conditions: SwiftShader (headless Chromium, --use-angle=swiftshader), 1366x768, the benchmark's street route and the house interior (src/engine/bench.js routes, their own camera), Quality Medium by hand, automatic resolution off (factor 1); 'battery' = game.setBattery(true) on Medium. 6 warm-up frames, then timed frames: 'total' = G.frame(1/30, render) to gl.finish (1-pixel readPixels), 'submit' = the CPU part (G.frame returning). The machine was shared with other agents' runs: per-frame noise is +-30 %. Software rendering: relative only, never the laptop's fps. base = 8b89e90 (0.40.0 + morning check), cand = GFX-LOOK-2 (392b85d + re-bake 93b79cb).

counts_exact.note: the 6 fewer shadow draws on the street come from the new sun direction (shadowcull.js sweeps each caster's shadow away from the sun; ?oldsun gives back 23); the 444 fewer triangles are those shadow draws

sequential_runs_ms_total_median_of_8_fra.reading: the interior's shaders and geometry are the same in both builds (only the fill light's colour differs), yet its medians differ by up to 25 % between runs: the machine's load. Sequential runs cannot resolve the change.

interleaved_frame_by_frame_ratio_cand_ov.method: one browser, two pages (base and candidate); each timed frame of one is followed by the same frame of the other; median of 10 per-frame ratios; run twice with the pages' order swapped
interleaved_frame_by_frame_ratio_cand_ov.reading: geometric means 1.00 / 0.97 / 1.03 / 1.10 (the last on an interior whose shaders did not change: noise). No difference SwiftShader can resolve. The one per-pixel change is in the terrain's splat shader: ~12 ALU operations for the paving's and the rock's re-split, no new texture read (the rock and grass samples it uses were already read).
